title: Workspace setup
prompt:
Design the first-run owner experience, titled “Welcome to Hamnivo”. A narrow three-step progress rail reads Workspace, Connect, Invite. Show Connect selected, with completed Workspace carrying a small check. This is step 2 of 3, not an endless setup wizard. The main panel says “Connect your first website” with a short sentence explaining that the customer widget appears after installation. Workspace is “Northline Studio”, with a discreet Demo badge. Three large but compact selectable rows: Website snippet, Package install, Help from a teammate. Select Website snippet. Beneath them place a labeled Website URL field with https://northline.example, a compact three-line JavaScript code block containing a fictional PUBLIC_DEMO_ID, a Copy snippet action and a “Where does this go?” disclosure. The key action is an ink “Verify installation” button. Include Back and “Finish later” links. A right-side preview occupying only one-third of the workspace shows the customer widget greeting and the brand icon. Avoid a huge illustration or empty hero area.
Use three focused state crops: successful check with “Widget detected” and “Continue to invite”; failed verification with “We couldn’t find the widget” and concrete checks for domain and code placement plus Retry; and invitation entry with “Invite teammates”, email input, role selector, Add another, and Send invites. Make invitation optional. Indicate that a role can be changed later. The core UX communicates progress, one next action, reversible setup, and an easy exit without discarding completed steps.

title: Sign-in and account recovery
prompt:
Create the authentication and recovery screen family. The main viewport is an intentionally restrained sign-in page with the Hamnivo logo in the top left, a thin footer containing Help and Privacy, and a centered compact card. Title “Sign in to your workspace”. Put a prominent ink “Continue with passkey” button first, an email field prefilled with amina@northline.example, then “Continue with email”. Beneath a quiet divider add “Continue with your company SSO”. Show “Use another workspace” as a text link and “Northline Studio” as the current workspace chip. This is a functional sign-in screen; do not fill the remainder with charts, testimonials or invented security claims. A small side illustration can use the H mark only, with ample but deliberate breathing room.
Three supporting crops cover practical recovery. First: a six-digit verification code panel, with code entry, “Code expired. Request a new code.”, Resend code and Back; never display an actual secret. Second: “Recover access” with options “Use a recovery code” and “Contact your workspace admin”, plus an explanation that changes may take review. Third: an in-app session-expired dialog above a muted inbox, “Your session ended”, a Sign in again action and “Your unsent draft is saved on this device.” Include a small device/session list row with This device, Last active now, and a Revoke action on another session. No authentication method should appear selected implicitly without a user action.

title: Widget appearance editor
prompt:
Render the workspace admin’s widget appearance editor. Maintain Hamnivo’s global shell. Header: “Customer widget”, tabs Appearance, Content, Behavior, Install. Appearance is selected. A compact editor column on the left occupies approximately 40 percent; a live website preview occupies the right 60 percent. Editor sections include Brand, Launcher, Conversation and Accessibility. Greeting is “How can we help today?” and supporting line “Ask a question or talk to the team.” Include an avatar visibility toggle, system/light/dark theme selection, and desktop/mobile preview switch.
The preview shows a plausible fictional online store page with a widget open; keep surrounding content very muted so the editor remains clear. A sticky action bar reads “Unsaved changes”, Reset and ink Publish. Add “Last published 26 Sep 2026” below the title.
Three state callouts: color validation explaining “This text color is difficult to read” with a darker accessible suggestion and Apply; unsaved-changes exit dialog with Keep editing and Discard changes; successful publication toast “Widget appearance published” with Undo. A mobile preview crop can be included inside the main preview pane, using the same widget. Editing should visibly update the preview without implying changes are live until Publish is used.

title: Customer conversation widget
prompt:
Create three customer-facing widget states at readable mobile scale, each showing only the product interface without phone hardware. Exterior labels: “Start a conversation”, “Get a useful answer”, “Send a file”. The customer is browsing Northline Studio’s fictional service website.

Show a private-information hint only where relevant: “Please don’t include payment card details.” Composer supports text, attach and send. The selected attachment has a visible upload progress status and Cancel; keep the customer’s unsent text intact. Match header height, bubble spacing, timestamps and composer position across all three screens.

title: Message delivery and offline recovery
prompt:
Create three mobile customer conversation views with exterior labels “Connection lost”, “Retry delivery”, and “Team is offline”. Each screen shares exactly the same chat header, bubbles and composer design as the main widget, making the state differences easy to compare.
First view: header “Northline Support”, a calm amber-tinted banner “You’re offline. We’ll send when you reconnect.” Show the customer’s latest message “Please check order NL-1048” with a small clock and Queued label. The message remains readable and there is no fake delivered check. Composer remains usable, with local draft “I can share the receipt too”. A compact “Trying to reconnect…” status appears in the banner. Avoid alarming full-screen error art.
Second view: restored connection, but one attachment message failed. Beneath that specific bubble show “Couldn’t send this file” with Retry and Remove actions; the surrounding conversation is still available. The text draft is preserved. Include an upload retry progress ring in one small row. A successful earlier message uses a modest Delivered label, not an ambiguous double check with unexplained color. A collapsed “Message details” entry gives sent time only when asked.
Third view: team is outside working hours. Explain “The team is offline. Leave your question and we’ll reply by email.” Show next availability “Monday, 9:00 AM · Dubai time” as a demo configuration rather than a service promise. Offer AI help now and a small follow-up form containing email, message, consent checkbox for conversation updates, and Send message. After submission, show a compact in-place acknowledgment with Edit email and Back to chat. Errors always have a next action and never erase the customer’s work.

title: Human and AI handoff
prompt:
Show a conversation being handed from AI to a human with explicit, understandable control. Main desktop screenshot uses the agent conversation workspace. The conversation header shows Sara N., “Human requested”, and assignment queue Support. A compact participant strip displays Sara · Customer, Support AI · Paused, Amina · Joining. Customer message reads “Please let me talk to a person.” The next public system message says “I’ve asked the team to join. Your conversation will stay here.” No artificial wait-time promise. The agent gets a concise handoff summary card: Request: change delivery address; Verified: order NL-1048 is preparing; Needs confirmation: new address; Actions taken: status checked only. Include Open full conversation. This is a summary of recorded facts, never hidden reasoning.
The right panel “Conversation control” states “Public replies: Amina” and “AI assistance: Draft suggestions only”. A secondary Invite specialist button opens choices Billing assistant and Shipping assistant; these remain private helpers unless explicitly granted customer-facing access. The main action is “Join and take over”. Below it make the relevant context scope clear: “Share this conversation from the last customer request”.
State crops: customer widget after a human joins with “Amina joined the conversation” and a human avatar; participant invitation dialog with role, visibility and history scope; and “Resume AI replies?” confirmation that requires an explicit action and explains which agent will speak. An activity line “AI reply cancelled when Amina took over” shows a safe takeover outcome. Make the human request a direct handoff path, not something an AI confidence score can veto. Use calm status colors and strong labels.

title: Typed decision rules
prompt:
Design an admin screen titled “Decision rules” with a clear subtitle “Classify requests and suggest the next step”. Within a selected rule “Human handoff”, show provider “Jev” in a small configuration chip and status Connected; never present the provider as ultimate authority. The main layout has a simple decision form on the left and a simulation panel on the right. Fields: Question “Does this request need a human?”, result type Choice, allowed choices Continue with AI, Ask for clarification, Route to human. Below the form show a distinct “Policy checks” section with rows “Customer asks for a person → Always route”, “Payment dispute → Route to Billing”, and “Decision unavailable → Ask a human”. Primary action Test rule; secondary Save draft.
State crops: typed result validation error with “Unexpected choice returned; fallback used”; provider timeout with “Decision service unavailable — routed to Support”; and an audit record showing input scope, result, policy applied, time and reviewer without secrets or hidden reasoning. Use a restrained coral accent for the selected path, not a flashy flowchart. The interface should make the distinction between a suggestion and permission obvious.
